panel_kit.material: kit_panel (single 2048^2 atlas: albedo JPEG, normal PNG, ORM PNG)
panel_kit.coords: glTF Y-up. Wall pieces: x 0..W, y 0..H, z 0 (outside face, +Z normal) .. -T (room side). Accessories (balcony*, entrance_canopy) start at the wall face z=0 and extend to +Z.

notes.wall_*_intact: exactly fills [0,W]x[0,H]x[-T,0] -> game normalisation offset is zero
notes.damage_states: all four states share the intact frame; damaged/holed/destroyed may protrude to +Z (curtains, rebar, door leaves, balcony stub) and -Z (room-side debris, radiators) by design
notes.wall_balcony_holed: includes the broken-off root of the balcony slab (game removes balcony_slab at state>=2)
notes.balcony_slab: mixed corrugated asbestos parapet + residents' glazing (wood/PVC/boarded). Variants balcony_slab_open, balcony_slab_glazed are extra (same placement rules) for the game to randomise
notes.balcony_hanging: hinge (wall face, slab top) is at local y = bbox_max.y - 0.14 relative to bbox min; game normalises minY=0 so place it at floor_y - (bbox height - 0.14) to keep the hinge at the slab line
notes.entrance_canopy: slab bottom at bbox minY+0.06 (lamp housing hangs 6 cm below the slab)
notes.roof_parapet: height 0.72 m + galvanised cap; roofing upturn on the room side (-Z)
notes.slab_floor: 3.2 x 0.22 x 3.2 m (x, y, -z). Top = linoleum, bottom = whitewashed ceiling. slab_floor_broken: outer half hinged down 35 deg on its bottom rebar
notes.stair_core: 3.2 wide x 2.8 high x 4.5 deep: flight up from z=-4.2 (floor landing provided by slab_floor) to the half-landing at y=1.4 against the facade, second flight back up to y=2.8
notes.plinth: 3.2 x 0.9 x 0.45 basement plinth with vent grille, same pivot rules as walls
notes.partition_wall_*: interior gypsum partition 3.2 x 2.58 x 0.08 with doorway; _intact/_holed
notes.debris_*: loose furniture debris (wardrobe, bed, table+chair, radiator), origin on the floor

rubble.notes: origin = ground centre of the pile, +Y up. One mesh per file, material "debris" (1024^2 atlas). rubble_1 big panel-fragment pile, rubble_2 brick-heavy pile, rubble_3 collapsed floor slabs "tent", rubble_4 low street debris, rubble_5 loose panel slab with rebar, rubble_6 brick scatter.

trees.notes: Top-level nodes laid out 9 m apart along +X (game uses each node as a template). Origin at trunk base. Names avoid matching two city.js classes: bare=tree_*, leafy=leafy_summer_*, stump_*, fallen_trunk. Materials: bark_<species> (tiling), wood_splintered, leaves_late_summer (alpha MASK 0.5, double sided), soil.

wires.notes: Poles: origin at ground, wire run along local +X, crossarm along local Z; attach_* empties are children of the pole node, positions given in pole-local glTF coords. utility_pole_broken: snapped at 1.3 m, top hanging on rebar (attach points follow the fallen top - the game should treat it as a broken pole). trolleybus_pole: attach_0 = span-wire strain insulator (6.9 m, road side +Z), attach_1 = feeder (6.25 m). concertina_coil: 6 m stretched coil along X, 0.9 m dia; barbed_wire_fence: 3 m segment along X with one snapped strand.

props.notes: One material (props_atlas 2048^2). Origin = ground centre of footprint, forward +Z, nodes laid out on a grid in the file. garage_unit* are 3.6 m wide modules (city.js places 4 side by side at 3.6 m) with doors to +Z. crater_* are positive meshes (ejecta rim + scorched bowl texture down to y=0.02, nothing below ground). car_vaz2107_wreck_side lies on its side.

module.why: 3.2 m is the transverse-wall step of II-49 / 1-464 variants and the contract grid of src/world/buildings.js; 2.8 m storey is the contract value (real 1-464: 2.5 m clear + 0.2 m slab ~ 2.7 m, II-49: 2.64-2.8 m) - kept for gameplay clearance and because every kit piece tiles on it.

openings_m.format: x0, y0, x1, y1 in panel coords (sill 0.86 m, head 2.30 m)

panel_section_m.note: three-layer panel; the broken-edge texture and geometry rings follow these layer depths

series.1-464 (khrushchyovka, 4-5 storeys): large-panel, cross walls of room size; WHE report 55 gives storey height 2.7 m, cross-wall span 2.7 / 3.6 m, room-size wall and floor panels, welded then monolithic joints (source: World Housing Encyclopedia report 55, Series 122/135/1-464c). Facades: small glazed ceramic tile on the panels, dark mastic in the joints, a coloured tile band under the windows; no lift, low parapet, flat roof.
series.1-468 / 1-480 (Ukrainian khrushchyovka/b: same 3.2 m step family, 5 and 9 storeys, 3-layer external panels 0.30-0.35 m (concrete / mineral wool / concrete), balconies on hanging slabs with steel railings and corrugated asbestos-cement parapet sheets.
series.II-49 / II-18 (9-12 storeys): step 3.2 m, storey ~2.64-2.8 m, single- or 3-layer ceramsite-concrete panels ~0.3 m, lift machine rooms and parapets on the roof, entrance canopies (precast slab on steel tie rods) over each stair door, stairwell windows at the half-landing.
details used: double wooden casements with a "fortochka" vent, white paint peeling; replacement white PVC units
balconies glazed by residents with mismatched wood/PVC frames, boarded panes, corrugated asbestos sheets
steel entrance door with intercom, concrete canopy, basement plinth with vent grilles
paper-tape crosses on window glass (blast protection), OSB boards over blown-out windows

war_damage_reference (Mariupol, Bakhmut,: black soot plumes rising from window heads after apartment fires, licking the reveals
shell penetrations through the spandrel merging with window openings, broken edges showing the insulation layer
hanging and bent rebar mesh, chunks still tied to bars, rebar of balcony roots dangling
facade tiles blown off around impacts, dense shrapnel pockmarks with light chipped halos, diagonal cracks from opening corners
pancaked vertical slices and collapsed top corners: stubs of lower panels with bars sticking up, slabs hinged down
debris fans at the base: panel fragments, bricks, window frames, radiators, furniture, insulation
shrapnel-stripped trees: snapped limbs, splintered trunks, a few still in leaf; pollarded city poplars
concrete SV-95 utility poles with pin insulators and cobra-head lamps; trolleybus span wires cut and hanging
research.note: All geometry/textures are procedurally generated by the scripts in tools/blender/env (no third-party assets).
